desc:
The string s has even length n and consists of exactly n / 2 characters '[' and n / 2 characters ']'.

It is balanced when every '[' can be paired with a later ']' and every ']' with an earlier '[', each bracket used once.

In one move you may choose any two indices (not necessarily adjacent) and swap the characters there. Return the minimum number of moves needed to make s balanced.

For example, "][][" needs one move: swap the first and last characters to get "[][]".
constraints: The number of [ equals the number of ]
hints: Which brackets are already fine and can be ignored? Cancel every [ with a later ].
What is left after cancelling is a block of ] followed by a block of [, and both blocks have the same size k because the totals are equal.
One swap can repair two stray closing brackets at once: swap an early stray ] with a late stray [. So the answer is ceil(k / 2).
editorial: Scan left to right with a counter of open brackets and count the number of ']' that arrive while the counter is 0; call it k. These are the unmatched closing brackets. Because the string has equally many brackets of both kinds, exactly k unmatched opening brackets remain at the end, so the leftover is ]^k [^k.

A swap of a stray ] at the front with a stray [ at the back turns them into a matched pair around everything in the middle, and repairs one stray of each kind per swap. The two innermost strays ], [ in the middle can be fixed in a single swap too, each swap fixing up to two strays on the closing side. Following that scheme the minimum is (k + 1) // 2. Time O(n), space O(1).
